M02.reason: The read-domain reset branch has inverted polarity, so the read pointer and underflow are reset while i_rst_n_rd=1 and run free while it is 0.

M03.reason: The pending-delay countdown completes on the wrong count, so the extra latency of the metastability model is wrong.

M04.reason: While the read side is blocked, o_empty_thr would be 0 instead of 1, which breaks o_empty=1 implying o_empty_thr=1.

M05.reason: The read FSM would leave ACK only when the synchronized write pointer is non-zero, so the flush check is inverted and the read release is wrong.

M06.reason: With +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN given, the enable meaning is inverted, so EN=0 would leave the random-latency model on and EN=1 would give nominal latency.

M07.reason: The write FSM would leave REL when either the ack is low or the read pointer is 0, so busy can fall before the full handshake and flush check complete.

M08.reason: The write-domain reset branch has inverted polarity, so write state is held in reset while i_rst_n_wr=1.

M09.reason: The read FSM would leave ACK when the request is low or the write pointer is 0, so the read release happens too early (before the write side is flushed).

M10.reason: The ack flop would reset to 1, so a read-domain hardware reset (alone, or while the write side is already released) presents a false acknowledge. A write FSM in REQ would then move to PTR before the read side has taken the request. The base run does not exercise it.

M12.reason: The synthesis 2FF cell would reset with inverted polarity, so the chain is cleared when RN=1 and shifts during reset.

M13.reason: The macro read register would only load when REB=1, but the wrapper drives REB=0, so o_rd_data never updates.

M14.reason: The write pointer would not advance on an accepted write, so every word overwrites entry 0 and full never rises.

M15.reason: The request flop would be 1 in every state except PTR, so the read side sees a software reset request even without one.

M16.reason: The pending-delay branch runs only when nothing is pending, so delayed changes are never delivered, or are delivered at the wrong time.

M17.reason: The read block condition is wrong: reads are blocked in normal RUN and unblocked during the software reset.

M18.reason: o_sw_rst_busy would reset to 1 instead of 0, so it is high during and after hardware reset.

M19.reason: A delayed change would not be marked pending, so it is never delivered to the output and the flag never moves.

M20.reason: The synthesis 2FF cell would reset its chain to 1 instead of 0, so the synchronized pointer reads non-zero after reset.

M21.reason: The read FSM would leave RUN when no request is present instead of when one arrives, so the software reset request is not taken and an unrequested reset is run.

M22.reason: The zero-extra-delay branch is chosen for the wrong cases, so the latency distribution of the model (S to S+2) is wrong.

M23.reason: The read pointer would not advance on an accepted read, so the same word is read repeatedly and empty never rises.

M24.reason: The read pointer would be cleared in every state except RST, so it is held at 0 in normal operation and not reset by the software reset.

M25.reason: The write FSM would leave REL exactly when the flush check is not met, so busy falls too early or never.

M29.reason: The write FSM would leave REL only when the synchronized read pointer is non-zero, so the flush check is inverted and busy does not fall correctly.
